stemBlocks.value: Think first: Deal with the numbers and each letter separately — the fraction is a single product on the top and a single product on the bottom.

solutionSteps.instruction: Divide the m parts using the index law.

strategyBlocks.value: Divide the numerical coefficients, then subtract the indices of m and of n.

whyThisWorks.value: Dividing powers of the same base subtracts the indices, because m² ÷ m is just (m × m) ÷ m with one factor of m cancelling. Splitting the fraction into a number part, an m part and an n part works since multiplication can be reordered freely. When an index difference reaches zero, that letter disappears entirely, which is why no n survives here.

commonErrors.misconception: Writing the answer as 2mn, forgetting that n ÷ n = 1 removes n completely.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Writing the answer as 2mn, forgetting that n ÷ n = 1 removes n completely.
